clue.text: An extra dance of an unpretentious nature?

definitions.meaning: in cricket a delivery bowled illegally gives the batting side an extra run
a modest dance that is not a grand ball at all, read playfully

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket extra conceded for an illegal delivery, and jokingly a dance too humble to count as a formal ball.

clue.text: Unbroken play direction

definitions.meaning: smooth and connected, without breaks between notes
an instruction to a performer on how to play a passage

explanation.definitionFit: A musical marking telling the performer to play smoothly, notes joined without breaks.

clue.text: A meeting that should be relatively convivial

definitions.text: A meeting that should be relatively convivial

parts.words: A meeting that should be relatively convivial
parts.note: relatively is a pun: the get-together is of relatives, and it ought to be friendly

explanation.surface: A get-together that ought to be fairly friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A reunion of relations, where kin assemble and are expected to be sociable.

clue.text: Assemblage of rope for censure

indicators.note: an assemblage puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for how they put a rope together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assemblage of' rearranges ROPE and FOR together.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, the same as censure or criticism.

clue.text: MPs who have qualified as MBs?

definitions.text: MPs who have qualified as MBs?

parts.words: MPs who have qualified as MBs?
parts.note: MPs are members of the House; an MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, so these members are doctors too, in hospital posts

explanation.surface: Politicians who also hold medical degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain MB is the basic medical degree, and these are junior hospital doctors who live in or work at the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Resident hospital doctors, jokingly pictured as Commons members with medical degrees.

clue.text: A trim sort of snare for a strict disciplinarian

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so A and trim are jumbled

parts.note: a net is a trap or snare

explanation.surface: Someone neat sets a trap, which suits a stickler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges A and TRIM to give MARTI.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a stickler for rules, demanding rigid obedience, like a harsh drill sergeant.

clue.text: Go off and become a cynic, apparently

definitions.meaning: a cynic is sour in outlook, so becoming one is read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Milk that spoils curdles, and a person who grows bitter or disillusioned is said to sour.

clue.text: Domestic security — it's the last thing voyagers want to get!

definitions.text: it's the last thing voyagers want to get

parts.note: a safe is a strongbox giving security

explanation.surface: Household security is what travellers hope to come back to.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is ironic: arriving back unharmed is the final thing travellers want, at the very end of the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Returned unharmed at the end of a journey, the hoped-for final outcome for travellers.

clue.text: Obscure part of shop a queue forms in

indicators.note: only a stretch of the following words supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A line of customers forms in a dim corner of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs inside 'shop a queue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opaque is unclear or hard to understand, so obscure fits.

clue.text: Turn up outside a Pyrenaen city

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter given by a
to turn something round makes it read the other way, so up is reversed

explanation.surface: A city in the Pyrenees comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' makes UP into PU, and 'outside' puts it round A. Pyrenaen is how the clue was printed, for Pyrenean.
explanation.definitionFit: Pau is a town in south-west France at the foot of the Pyrenees mountains.

clue.text: Supercilious chartered accountant with a liver disorder

indicators.note: putting into disorder jumbles the letters of a and liver

explanation.surface: An arrogant accountant suffers from a liver complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges A and LIVER to give VALIER. 'disorder' reads as a medical ailment but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is offhand and haughty, showing disdain like a supercilious one.

clue.text: Glossy fabrics ruined by stains, possibly

indicators.note: wrecked letters are rearranged, so stains is jumbled

explanation.surface: Shiny dress materials spoilt by marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges STAINS; 'possibly' just marks it as a cryptic suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth, lustrous woven cloth, so the plural names shiny materials.

clue.text: One who isn't at all happy to go along with us

definitions.text: One who isn't at all happy to go along with us

parts.words: One who isn't at all happy to go along with us
parts.note: a fellow traveller who is miserable, read as someone reluctant to agree with us

explanation.surface: Someone who is reluctant to agree with our plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go along with' sounds like agreeing, but it means accompanying: the companion keeps us company while being glum.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserable person who keeps you company, a sad and morose sort of associate.

clue.text: Have won another order

indicators.note: putting the letters in another order rearranges the word won

explanation.surface: Have we won a fresh command?
explanation.walkthrough: 'another order' rearranges WON.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it, the verb sense of the answer.

clue.text: A weather-beaten old-timer

parts.note: an ancient timekeeping device left out in all weathers in the garden

explanation.surface: A grizzled veteran exposed to the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-timer' suggests a veteran person, but it is an old device for telling the time, which stands outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden clock telling the hour by a shadow, exposed to wind and rain for years.

clue.text: Books in this state are clearly quite unreadable

definitions.text: Books in this state are clearly quite unreadable

parts.words: Books in this state are clearly quite unreadable
parts.note: a volume whose covers or pages have not been parted cannot be read

explanation.surface: Some books are impossible to read in their present condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreadable' suggests bad writing, but it simply means the book has never been opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Never having been opened, a book's pages cannot be seen, so it cannot be read.

clue.text: Sauce for the wounded soldier?

definitions.meaning: a liquid topping, as on a salad
a bandage applied to an injury

explanation.definitionFit: A salad topping such as vinaigrette, and also a bandage put on a wound.

clue.text: They won't let on they are natives

definitions.text: They won't let on they are natives

parts.words: They won't let on they are natives
parts.note: natives is a name for cultivated shellfish from British beds, which clam up and never reveal anything

explanation.surface: Locals who keep quiet about where they come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'natives' are British-bred shellfish, especially those from Whitstable; they stay tight-lipped, as closed shells.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives is the trade name for bivalve molluscs raised in British waters, famously closed and silent.

clue.text: Are taken up for a number of years

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking a word up reads it from bottom to top, so are is backwards

explanation.surface: Things are adopted for some years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' reverses ARE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, a span of many years.

clue.text: Devises something entirely new in outlets?

parts.note: vents are openings that let out air or gas

explanation.surface: Someone comes up with original designs for openings.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is given as written, followed by VENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent is to create a novel thing, as an inventor devises a new machine.

clue.text: What the prudent conjurer might well have to fall back on?

definitions.text: What the prudent conjurer might well have to fall back on?

parts.words: What the prudent conjurer might well have to fall back on?
parts.note: a magician keeps a hidden item palmed, and a careful person keeps a reserve for emergencies

explanation.surface: A careful magician keeps a backup trick ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a reserve kept back; for a conjurer it is literally an object concealed in the palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve or spare kept back, and literally an object a magician holds concealed in the palm.

clue.text: Rugger man who meets with success as an angler

definitions.meaning: a rugby forward in the front row who heels the ball back in the scrum

definitions.text: who meets with success as an angler
definitions.meaning: a fisherman who catches fish on the line

explanation.definitionFit: A rugby front-row forward, and a fisherman who lands a catch on the line.

clue.text: An upheaval about a habit that produces revulsion

indicators.note: the reversed word and the following a go round the word for habit
heaving a word up in a down entry turns it over, so an is read backwards

parts.note: use is custom or habit, as in long use

explanation.surface: A commotion over a custom that disgusts people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheaval' turns AN into NA; 'about' puts NA and A round USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is a feeling of sickness and disgust, the same as revulsion.

clue.text: Terse review about a ticklish problem

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter given by a
to review is to go over again and recast, so terse is rearranged

explanation.surface: A curt critique concerning a tricky issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' rearranges TERSE into TESER, and 'about' puts it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky question, a delicate problem to solve.

clue.text: Close of play, perhaps

parts.note: the final speech at the end of a drama, not the end of a day's cricket

explanation.surface: Stumps being drawn at the end of the day's sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close of play' is a cricket phrase for stumps, but here play means a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A closing speech or section after the main action of a drama or book.

clue.text: An Alpine flower the traveller's joy it could be!

definitions.meaning: flower read as something that flows: a river of the Alps

definitions.text: the traveller's joy it could be!
definitions.meaning: a roadside hostelry offering a weary traveller food and a bed; traveller's joy is also a plant name

explanation.definitionFit: A river rising in Switzerland and flowing through Austria, and a hostelry welcoming travellers.

clue.text: Standard author not translated into French?

parts.note: to author is to write, or pen, a work
non is the French word for no or not

explanation.surface: A classic writer whose work was never rendered in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective, but it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag, and a standard is a banner or flag.

clue.text: Offered to look after a collection of deer

parts.note: to tend is to look after or care for

indicators.note: collecting the letters together in a new heap rearranges the word deer

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to care for a herd of deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a collection of' rearranges DEER into ERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something is to present or offer it, as in tendering a resignation.
